title: Scan commits, publications, and mirrors for secrets and malware
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Scan commits, publications, and mirrors for secrets and malware
events.body:
## Outcome

Use one bounded scanner across local hooks, publication, and mirror intake so risky content is caught before replication whenever possible.

## Implementation

- Create a shared scanner interface for secret fingerprints, private-key formats, malware rules, and operator-supplied detectors.
- Provide opt-in pre-commit hook installation plus mandatory configurable pre-push or pre-publish evaluation.
- Scan newly fetched public objects before a mirror advertises them and quarantine failures through #450.
- Log only rule identifiers, fingerprints, paths, and locations; never log matching secret bytes.
- Require an explicit signed local override and show that redaction cannot be guaranteed after data has replicated.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same fixture produces the same decision in hook, publish, and mirror paths.
- Private ciphertext is not mis-scanned before authorized decryption.
- A clean replacement clears quarantine only after a complete rescan.
- Overrides are scoped, expiring, auditable, and cannot silently disable other rules.
- Scanner time, memory, file count, and object size are bounded for hostile input.

## Dependencies

Integrates with the node-local policy engine in #450.

## Verification

Seed secret, malware, binary, oversized, renamed, deleted, encrypted, overridden, and cleaned fixtures through each entry point and scan all diagnostics for the original match bytes.
